headline: Broad-Based Growth with Margin Headwinds

highlights: Key Points  Revenue stood below our estimate at Rs15.0bn, while EBITDA declined 12.7% YoY to Rs839mn, with margins down ~170bps to 5.6%.

In commercial washers, IFB continues to lead the domestic market with a 20–25% share, generating Rs1.04bn revenue in FY26.  The refrigerator business is gradually gaining traction, with IFB focusing on premium, frost-free models and targeting at least 33% of sales from this category.

Rs32.3mn last year), owing to an 8–10% increase in oil-based raw material costs amid geopolitical tensions.  Management targets ~20% FY27 growth in Home Appliances (vs. 14.5% in H1), with a strong Q3 expected on festive demand.
It aims to improve EBITDA margins towards 10% through cost efficiencies and calibrated pricing.

Three levers still underpin the thesis: SKU economization (front- loader models cut from ~57 to 25, washer SKUs from ~100 to ~50), sustained overhead reduction (Rs1.50bn targeted for FY27 via headcount discipline and volume-linked trade schemes, though H1 progress wasn’t quantified on this call), and the portfolio (higher-capacity RACs, a targeted 7-10% AC market share).

On the distribution front, IFB is prioritising weighted distribution, focusing on visibility and throughput at key outlets rather than merely expanding store count.
